methods.label: List the possible lineups
methods.explanation:
Use the usual random-lineup interpretation, in which every order is equally likely. Label the students \(X,Y,Z\) in alphabetical order of their names. Their possible orders from front to back are
\[
XYZ,\ XZY,\ YXZ,\ YZX,\ ZXY,\ ZYX.
\]
This list is complete: each of the three students appears first in two listed orders, covering both ways to arrange the remaining students. No order appears twice.

Only \(XYZ\) is alphabetical. Thus the probability is
\[
\frac{\text{alphabetical orders}}{\text{all orders}}=\frac16.
\]
The answer is \(\frac16\), choice C.
